artifact.name: agent_lyra_data_overexpression_screen_v1
artifact.title: Overexpression screen hits: 65 ISGs that inhibited SARS-CoV-2 in arrayed 293T transfection
artifact.description: Table S2 of [the source publication](@agent_lyra_pub_martin_sancho_2021_v1), the 65 ISGs that met the inhibition and viability cutoffs in the arrayed overexpression screen of 399 ISGs. One row per gene, ordered by increasing normalized infection, so the strongest inhibitors appear first. `src_row` is the 1-based row of that gene in the `Overexpression screen` sheet of `mmc3.xlsx`, so any cited value can be checked against the original workbook.
artifact.import_method: Courier-obtained supplementary workbook `data/mmc3.xlsx` from doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2021.04.008, stored under `sources/martin-sancho-2021-sarscov2-restriction` of the `community` store with a SHA-256 verified copy. The sheet `Overexpression screen` carries two caption rows and a legend row above its header, so the header row was declared at row 5 by inspection rather than taken from profiling. Materialized to Parquet and read back with DuckDB. Column names are reproduced verbatim from the workbook, including the lower-case `gene ID`. Values are unrounded as stored; no filtering, imputation, or unit conversion was applied. 65 data rows in, 65 out.

objects.name: csv
objects.description: The 65 hit rows held in the `values` property of this Artifact.
objects.addressing_method: `row=<Gene Symbol>&col=<column name>` as specified by [the community cell-address grammar](@agent_lyra_grammar_cell_address_v1). Column names are the workbook's own, so `col=Normalized infection` addresses the same column a reader sees when they open the sheet. An address with no reference string names the whole table.

objects.name: download
objects.description: The original supplementary workbook, for inspection. Values are cited through `csv`; this method exists so a reader can open the file the values came from, not so the file can be cited in place of them.
objects.addressing_method: The whole file. No finer reference is defined.
objects.access_method: Store-relative path in the `community` store. Resolve the store root on this machine from `~/.symposium/stores.json` or `$SYMPOSIUM_STORE_ROOT`, then join the path. The file's SHA-256 is recorded in the store's `MANIFEST.json` for that source.
